scope: Third pass on Shiori's engine: hayro's speed against PDFium, on a fork of hayro (bitemyapp/hayro, branch aizome-perf), after the first changes were split into upstream pull requests. Component evidence on a laptop and a shared workstation; not VM, ISO or hardware qualification. Shiori still draws with PDFium.
workstation: ganymede (Intel Core Ultra 7 365: 4 performance and 4 efficiency cores, 30 GiB RAM), shared with other sessions (one-minute load average 3-4)

method.program: the scratch benchmark of the earlier passes: each file in a process of its own under `timeout 30`, four files at a time, release builds, up to the first 5 pages at 2x on white, time per page including loading the page
method.change_from_earlier_passes: every process is pinned to the four performance cores (`taskset -c 0-3`); unpinned runs moved between core types and gave bimodal times. Absolute times are lower than in the earlier records, so compare ratios across records, not milliseconds
method.final_timings: PDFium 8066, hayro master 8558a8a5 and the fork's aizome-perf dfd3e753 ran back to back on each file, three times; each page's time is its median of the three
method.exactness: each change was compared with the build before it on every page of the corpus (pixel for pixel) and with hayro's own test suite; changes that alter pixels are listed with how much

not_proposed.glyph coverage cache: the maintainer wants to write glyph caching himself (hayro issue 1613)
not_proposed.block averaging before large downscales: dropped: slower than the SIMD resampler alone at moderate reductions (large_jpeg_downscale 43 to 54 ms), and the image cache already covers the one page it helped
not_proposed.the changes below: on the fork only so far

corrections_while_splitting.image cache key: now also covers a color space resolved by name from the resources and the active transfer function, which change how the same image stream decodes
corrections_while_splitting.mesh sampling area: clipping to the render context alone changed edge pixels (the texture repeats and is filtered across its edges); the area is the texture's bounds plus a pixel, and the result is pixel-identical to master
corrections_while_splitting.gradient table: 4,096 eagerly evaluated steps became 65,536 evaluated on first use, so a step stays under a pixel on gradients up to 65,536 pixels long; five corpus pages differ from master, by at most 1 level
corrections_while_splitting.luminance masks: 16-bit fixed point differed from vello's formula on 7,749 of the 2^24 colors; per-channel tables of the same float expression are exact on all of them

fork_changes_since_the_pull_requests.clip bounds: the renderer keeps the device-space bounds of the active clips; fills, strokes and images outside them are skipped, and shading and non-repeating pattern textures cover only what the clips let through (tiling-pattern-box: 240 to 83 ms)
fork_changes_since_the_pull_requests.shared color spaces and shadings: Separation, DeviceN and Indexed color spaces given by arrays, and shadings, are kept in the interpreter's object cache, so their lookup tables and functions are built once (bug1721218_reduced: 360 to 99 ms; PDFium 234)
fork_changes_since_the_pull_requests.patch mesh triangles: kept per shading and scale from their second use, each grid point's color interpolated once, and each patch cut into cells of about two device pixels instead of 19 by 19 (issue13520: 125 to 14 ms, PDFium 15; personwithdog: 131 to 75 ms, PDFium 78)
fork_changes_since_the_pull_requests.soft masks and pattern-filled stencils: drawn only within their group's bounds and the active clips, the rest filled with the background's value (issue18032: 77 to 18 ms; bug1795263: 46 to 6.6 ms, PDFium 6.3)
fork_changes_since_the_pull_requests.redundant clip rectangles: a clip rectangle covering everything visible is not pushed to vello_cpu (issue14297: 54 to 27 ms)
fork_changes_since_the_pull_requests.masked-image layers: an image with a soft mask of another size is drawn as a layer clipped to the image's whole-pixel bounds; vello_cpu otherwise composites its destination-in layer over the whole target (chrome-text-selection-markedContent: 78 to 13 ms)
fork_changes_since_the_pull_requests.CMaps: the predefined CMaps are embedded uncompressed (467 KB, 217 KB more), saving about 3 ms of brotli decompression for each document with a CID font
fork_changes_since_the_pull_requests.PostScript functions: the 100-entry stack is reused per thread instead of set up and moved for every evaluation (function_based_shading: 92 to 56 ms)
fork_changes_since_the_pull_requests.single-copy tiling patterns: when only one copy of a cell can be seen and the fill has no soft mask or blend mode, the cell is drawn directly into the fill's clip at device resolution (tiling-pattern-box: 84 to 6.8 ms, PDFium 4.9)
fork_changes_since_the_pull_requests.JPEGs decoded no larger than drawn: JPEGs are decoded at 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 across and, separately, down, while the decoded image stays 1.5 times the drawn size, using reduced-size decoding added to zune-jpeg (below); 2x, three runs each, pinned: large_jpeg_downscale 46 to 19 ms (PDFium 20), 22060_A1_01_Plans 237 to 133 ms, and at 1/4 (a thumbnail) 225 to 59 ms. These were measured after the corpus totals above, which don't include the change; the corpus rerun on wx-workstation (results_with_reduced_size_jpegs) does

zune_jpeg.fork: https://github.com/bitemyapp/zune-image, branch scaled-idct, on zune-jpeg's development branch (0.5.16-rc3); hayro's fork depends on it by git until it's released
zune_jpeg.reduced_size_decoding: DecoderOptions::jpeg_set_scale_denominator(s) and JpegDecoder::output_dimensions: each block reconstructed by the decoder's inverse DCT and averaged (libjpeg's scale_denom computes the same means), a 1 by 1 block from its DC term alone, subsampled components reconstructed at the output's resolution so nothing is up-sampled; falls back to full size for DNL images and raw, planar and scanline output
zune_jpeg.against_libjpeg_turbo: djpeg -scale 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 on a photograph re-encoded by cjpeg: 4:4:4 and 4:2:0, baseline and progressive, within 0.3 levels on average (at most 3); 4:2:2, 4:4:0 and 4:1:1 within 1.3 (at most 30), where libjpeg up-samples chroma
zune_jpeg.robustness: every JPEG in zune-image's test images at every scale, and 13,500 truncated or corrupted variants (release and debug builds), without a panic
zune_jpeg.speed: 7680 by 4320 4:4:4: 62 ms at full size, 40 ms at 1/2, 24 ms at 1/8; Huffman decoding, about half of a full decode, is the floor
zune_jpeg.restart_regression: zune-jpeg's development branch tore grayscale JPEGs whose restart interval doesn't divide an MCU row (pdfbox 2244 in hayro's suite): a latched RST was handled at the end of a row with the segment's last MCUs still buffered. Bisected to babf5c25 (May 2026, after the 0.5.15 release); fixed with a test on the fork (branch fix-restart-across-rows, and in scaled-idct)
zune_jpeg.row_limit: JpegDecoder::set_row_limit (13f18bce, on scaled-idct): a sequential image whose first scan holds all its components decodes as though it were that many rows tall, stopping after the MCU row holding the last; a test checks the rows against the whole image's (exact more than 16 rows above the cut, where chroma isn't upsampled from undecoded rows). zune-jpeg's tests pass but for the failure already on its development branch
zune_jpeg.other_difference_from_0_5_15: a truncated JPEG in hayro's corpus/0942791 shows one fewer row of decoded padding, filled with neutral grey: the development branch's deliberate handling of incomplete data
zune_jpeg.not_proposed: neither branch has been proposed to zune-image yet

fork_changes_after_reduced_size_jpegs.range: 04aecd3c to ad5920e6 on aizome-perf; times pinned on wx-workstation, five or seven runs each, against the build before; instruction counts from callgrind where the machine was loaded
fork_changes_after_reduced_size_jpegs.DeviceCMYK table (833ab0b3): 36 corpus files built moxcms's CMYK transform the first time they used DeviceCMYK, about 7 ms each (269 ms in all, most on pages PDFium draws in under 5 ms). The 17^4 table moxcms builds is now an asset (250 KB), interpolated as its fixed-point executor does; a test checks it against moxcms on 6.8 million colors (identical on AMD and Intel). moxcms is three times faster per pixel once built, so after 2^19 pixels its transform is built and used instead. devicen-none-zero-domain 7.8 to 0.19 ms (PDFium 0.15); the 36 files 1,397 to 1,154 ms
fork_changes_after_reduced_size_jpegs.mesh sampling (1b2a797b, b949ec0d, 7b88d: a triangle covers one run of each row (each of kurbo's side tests changes sign at most once along a row), so runs are found from where the edges cross the row and their ends confirmed with the same test; weights are stepped along a run; runs are filled at a time; a mesh texture's rows are read as slices of the samples. issue2948: 852 to 238 million instructions, 50 to 18 ms (PDFium 8.0)
fork_changes_after_reduced_size_jpegs.premultiplied texels (1b2a797b): shading textures went through floats for every texel and were rounded again by the renderer; the gradient table now holds finished premultiplied texels and opaque gray and RGB meshes are quantized straight to bytes. radial_gradients 85 to 50 ms over its five pages (PDFium 59)
fork_changes_after_reduced_size_jpegs.glyph runs as one image (96f4ac00): each cached glyph was drawn with a rectangle of its own, a few thousand instructions in vello_cpu before any pixel; a run's cached glyphs now go into one coverage image drawn once. tracemonkey 46.5 to 38.5 ms (PDFium 39.4), and its seven variants alike
fork_changes_after_reduced_size_jpegs.decompressors per thread (12774fa1): every Flate stream set up a decompressor, zeroing a 32 KiB window (about 40,000 instructions, more than many small streams take); each thread now keeps one zlib and one deflate decompressor, with read_to_end's results (all of a stream, or nothing if it's corrupt or ends early). issue918 286 to 205 million instructions
fork_changes_after_reduced_size_jpegs.CMap destinations inline (dcea7506): each bf range's destination was a vector of its own, so parsing a predefined CMap allocated one per entry; destinations are now inline (SmallVec of 4). vertical_rotated_fallback_glyphs 139 to 76 million instructions, 8.4 to 6.9 ms
fork_changes_after_reduced_size_jpegs.invisible paints skipped (43b6164f): a paint whose every color is fully transparent, composited over the target, changes no pixel; fills, strokes, glyph runs and stencils with one aren't drawn. axial_shading_many_inputs (16 page-sized shadings whose function wants 18 inputs where one is given) 18.7 to 1.7 ms (PDFium 1.6)
fork_changes_after_reduced_size_jpegs.JPEG rows the page can show (a1666484): the renderer hints the image's last row that can be seen on the page (the page's bounds and clips, the same for every tile) plus 16, and JPEGs stop decoding after it (zune_jpeg row_limit below); only for images resampling won't make smaller, whose pixels a cut can't change, and without a mask of another stream. issue12841_reduced (a 5280 by 3792 photograph at 1:1, 39% of its rows on the page) 137 to 55 ms (PDFium 70)
fork_changes_after_reduced_size_jpegs.one-input mesh functions in a table (8c4: meshes whose colors are a function's values at one input evaluated it at every texel; texels now come from a table of the function at 65,536 inputs between the least and greatest sampled, as for axial and radial shadings. coons-allflags-withfunction 25.5 to 12.4 ms and tensor-allflags-withfunction 24.9 to 12.6 (PDFium 18); the only change of these that moves pixels on purpose, by 1 level
fork_changes_after_reduced_size_jpegs.tried and dropped: a lookup table for the CMap Huffman decoder (its codes are short, so walking the tree cost the same); cutting JPEGs that are resampled smaller (resampling depends on the height, so the whole image shifted by a fraction of a pixel)

fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.range: ad5920e6 to 72fd16cb on aizome-perf, chasing the pages still behind PDFium at ad5920e6; instruction counts from callgrind (the workstation was loaded), times pinned on wx-workstation
fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.zeroed pixmaps (51110ddc): vello_cpu's Pixmap::new fills its buffer; pixmaps are now made from zeroed vectors, which fresh memory gives without a pass. issue14497 (6740 by 4768 pixels) 38 to 21 ms rasterizing, now faster than PDFium (24 against 28 in all)
fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.patch cells (d9fd7044): each cell's second triangle takes its colors by move rather than clone, and triangle bounds are floored and ceiled with integers instead of libm calls (baseline x86-64 has no SSE 4.1 rounding). personwithdog 1,160 to 1,052 million instructions
fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.textures on whole pixels (29c5412e): a shading texture that's only moved by whole pixels has a texel at each pixel's center, so it's sampled without the bilinear filter, which would give the same values. issue2948 238 to 177 million instructions
fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.Type 3 glyphs cached (41d16a43): Type 3 glyphs that give a shape (d1) and draw only paths, clips and image masks are drawn once into coverage, cached as outline glyphs are and composited with the fill color. issue918 10.8 to 7.0 ms (PDFium 5.4). The only change of these that moves pixels (see quality)
fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.gradient steps (e6bc817e): gradient and mesh-function tables round their steps with integers instead of roundf. issue8092 154 to 135 million instructions
fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.soft-mask bounds (58e06566): a soft mask is drawn only within the bounds of what its group draws (paths, strokes widened by their reach, and images; text gives up), and one that's opaque everywhere is dropped. issue18894 58 to 41 million instructions, bug1703683_page2_reduced 269 to 241
fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.PostScript numbers (1298c895): numbers in PostScript functions are converted to f32 when parsed rather than at each evaluation. function_based_shading 1,020 to 1,006 million instructions
fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.CID widths as runs (bb300542): a W array's ranges were expanded into a hash map entry per CID (a range to 4294967295 would have taken all memory); runs of CIDs now keep a width each or one for all, searched by halves. issue9915_reduced 11 to 1 million instructions, 1.39 to 0.33 ms (PDFium 0.42); issue15096's font set-up 22.5 to 6.7 million
fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.ICC luminance transform when needed (d3f: every one-component ICC space built a second transform, for luminance soft masks, as it was created; it's now built when a soft mask needs it. bug793632 30 to 26 million instructions; issue15096's four ICC spaces 25.6 to 13.0 million
fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.gradient stops fitted once (72fd16cb): an axial or radial shading drawn as a native gradient had its stops fitted for every fill; they depend only on the shading, the pattern's opacity and transfer function, so they're kept with the shading, and a sample is reused where an interval's middle is a quarter of the one it halves. issue17065 (one OKLab shading through a PostScript function, filled nine times) 42 to 12 million instructions, 2.91 to 0.98 ms (PDFium 1.12)
fork_changes_after_ad5920e6.tried and dropped: building for x86-64-v3 (SSE 4.1 rounding, AVX2 and FMA everywhere): 2.7% over the pages PDFium drew (5,498 against 5,649 ms), not adopted since nixpkgs builds for baseline x86-64; precomputing the Bernstein weights of patch cells (LLVM already shared them)

remaining_gaps_to_pdfium.as_of: 72fd16cb; times are medians from results_at_fd143243 (the quieter runs) for pages the last three commits don't change. Of the gaps listed at ad5920e6, very large pages are closed (issue14497 24 ms against 28) and Type 3 image glyphs narrowed (issue918 7.7 against 5.7, the rest being each glyph's first drawing, with bicubic filtering)
remaining_gaps_to_pdfium.free-form and patch meshes: issue2948 (14.6 ms against 8.0): a pixel's weights and color for each triangle covering it, triangles overlapping. personwithdog (70.5 against 65.5): patches cut into cells of about two pixels, a CMYK conversion per pixel. issue6231_1 (7.6 against 4.5): a mesh colored by a stitching function, 37,800 evaluations of about 590 instructions each through the 65,536-step table, then an image paint of the texture
remaining_gaps_to_pdfium.soft masks and nested groups: bug1755507 (17.4 against 10.1, a JPEG inside a soft mask), issue12798_page1_reduced (9.7 against 4.7, nested transparency groups), issue5044 (4.7 against 2.6) and issue18894 (4.5 against 3.0): vello_cpu's layers, which clear a buffer per tile and composite masks pixel by pixel
remaining_gaps_to_pdfium.PostScript functions: function_based_shading (55.6 against 52.6) and colorspace_sin, _cos and _atan (10.8-12.4 against 9.3-11.4): a stack machine over tagged values, about 50 instructions an operation (issue17065's OKLab conversion, about 100 operations, took 5,100 instructions an evaluation). Compiling programs to straight-line code, or to per-operation closures, is what's left; these pages also swing most with code layout
remaining_gaps_to_pdfium.predefined CJK CMaps: vertical_rotated_fallback_glyphs (7.3 against 1.6) and pattern_text_rotated_fallback_glyphs (5.5 against 3.7): parsing the binary CMaps at first use, about 5 ms; PDFium compiles its in. The bcmap files hold one large segment per kind of entry, so decoding lazily doesn't help; tables built ahead of time and searched in place would
remaining_gaps_to_pdfium.color space set-up: issue10339_reduced (1.8 against 0.6) and issue2761 (3.3 against 2.4) each make a Lab space, whose moxcms transform (18 million instructions) builds the sRGB output curve as a table of 65,536 entries with a pow each; ICC spaces pay the same, about 3 million a transform (issue15096 builds four). The curve is the same for every transform, so a moxcms change to share it, or sharing transforms between identical profiles (not yet checked on the corpus), would remove most of it
remaining_gaps_to_pdfium.font set-up: issue16316 (4.3 against 2.8): parsing a Type 1 font, 10.8 million instructions
remaining_gaps_to_pdfium.smaller: issue8092 (10.8 against 8.0, shadings sampled through gradient tables), large_jpeg_downscale (18.0 against 16.2, JPEG decoding), text-heavy pages within a millisecond (tracemonkey and its variants, which move with memory layout)

not_covered: the fork isn't in Shiori; no VM or hardware runs; machines under shared load; JPEG 2000 pages were checked and are on par with PDFium (865 ms against 974 over the 14 corpus pages that have them)
